data.title: Domain
data.tagline: Give a website a human-readable address
data.description: A domain name is the address people type, such as example.com. It is registered separately from the server that hosts the site and points to that service through DNS. Renew it on time, protect the account, and decide which subdomains each service uses.

use: Point visitors to a deployed website
avoid: Assume buying a domain also creates the website
Change DNS records without knowing which service uses them
Put secret information in a domain or subdomain name

lessonPractice.title: You bought example.com, but opening it still does not show the website you built. What should be confirmed next?

options.label: Add example.com at the hosting platform but do not inspect its current DNS
options.feedback: The host may know the domain while DNS still points visitors to the registrar's parking page.

options.label: Confirm the site is deployed, then point DNS according to the host's instructions
options.feedback: A domain is only a name. A reachable host must serve the site, and DNS must connect the name to that service.

options.label: Forward the domain to a temporary address and let the browser navigate away
options.feedback: A redirect may open the site but changes the visible address and does not properly bind the custom domain.

data.agentPrompt: Find why example.com does not open the production site: confirm deployment, then check the host's domain binding and required DNS records. Do not change unrelated records or rely on URL forwarding. Verify example.com and HTTPS afterward.
